subject.title: fix(agents): bound base64 image input before decode in tool-image sanitizer

question: Should tool-output images above 10 MiB become an intentionally unsupported input class even when the sanitizer could resize them below its output limit?
rationale: Source and proof establish the OOM bug, but code evidence cannot decide the permanent compatibility tradeoff between bounded memory and preserving larger valid tool images.

options.title: Approve the 10 MiB ceiling
options.body: Treat larger tool-output images as unsupported, retain the visible text fallback, and add a valid near-boundary compatibility test before landing.

options.title: Scale the ceiling with the output budget
options.body: Derive a bounded pre-decode allowance from `maxBytes` with an absolute safety cap so configured or future larger output budgets retain resize headroom.

options.title: Pause for workload evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers establish the largest valid tool-image inputs that current integrations need to resize.

recommendation.title: Approve the 10 MiB ceiling
recommendation.body: Treat larger tool-output images as unsupported, retain the visible text fallback, and add a valid near-boundary compatibility test before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared base64 estimator and recent pre-decode media-budget work make this the strongest available owner signal for selecting the safety boundary.
